---
name: revise
description: Revise the neuron explanation, six analysis sections, figure captions and final Criticism from measured results.
disable-model-invocation: true
metadata:
  disco-role: operating

# Report

Read `/inputs/handoff/handoff.json`, its HTML and measurements. Read the condition registry for the actual full-prefix anchors, scoring definitions, ablations and contribution vectors. Use measured denominators from those records. Revise the explanation using the search, route clusters, gate/value anatomy, family, RelP circuit measurements and the semantic activation spectrum together.

Read the handoff as an overview: measurement_summary contains experiment status, key statistics and paths; complete measurements remain in the referenced files. Use scripts/read_evidence.py to read saved evidence by section or case, and use --section measurements to list experiments or --section measurements --ids EXPERIMENT_ID to read one experiment overview and its file names. For details, load the referenced JSON file in Python and print the fields needed for the question. Full texts, traces, contribution vectors and plotting arrays remain available in those files. The host renders the HTML from your submitted interpretation and annotations.

## References

- [API reference](references/api-reference.md): claim, Criticism and annotations.
- [Workflow](references/workflows.md): report submission.

## Write

For existing-data runs, read the saved coactivation and proposed text tests in the measurements. Describe neighbour associations using their sampled correlation and same-input traces. Semantic Clusters are groups of selected contexts. Neither supplies causal routes or upstream/downstream contributions. Proposed texts are internal experiment plans with no measured activation score; they are not publication sections. Discuss counterexamples and select a representative saved strip when helpful. The fixed tools fill direct output weights and numerical group counts.

Explain which observations support each pole and which suggest an alternative. Name the measured routes, describe representative gate/value traces, and annotate the figures and six analysis sections. Distinguish observed local RelP contributions, native neuron-zeroing effects and corpus associations. Circuit tables aggregate the natural atlas with downstream coverage limited to nominated same-position readers. New probes have separate attribution records and route assignments. Use their zeroing results and matched controls when revising the interpretation. Use the measured independent texts in Criticism, including failures to reach the corpus extreme. Route prediction is disabled in this pipeline; leave it as — and make no claim about its accuracy. Discuss semantic-group counts as counts of the selected samples. Keep the initial-version blind tests attached to the explanation they tested.

Match each figure's conclusion to its actual selected token or scored span, reading the saved native trace where needed. A flat response at one token does not imply inactivity across the sentence or refute a hypothesis about another position. Distinguish cue tokens, the boundary before an upcoming value and tokens within or after that value. Captions name the measured location and quantity; product is not raw gate. Preserve failed or uninformative tests and explain their scope. Prefer informative controlled contrasts and strong counterexamples for the main figures; keep flat diagnostic tests available without presenting magnified near-zero residuals as a strong effect.

Select exactly three representative measured graphs for Three graphs, using annotations.graph_ids in display order. Cover both observed poles and a distinct mechanism or informative counterexample. Additional measured graphs remain in the saved artifacts. Preserve the ten-condition common-frame headline selected with annotations.headline_figure_id; change that ID only to another measured ten-condition comparison covering the same evidence needs. Keep actual failed controls and measured signs. The ten-condition figures and eleven short family inputs are measured during the experiment stage; this stage supplies their explanation and captions.

Submit through `scripts/write_report.py`. Numerical fields are filled from the saved measurements. Default language is English; unavailable fields remain —. This stage runs no new experiments.

For each Criticism row choose exactly one verdict code: `survived` (the tested claim survived as written), `narrowed` (it needs qualification or revision), or `rejected` (it failed). Write the reasoning in `result` and the challenge in `attack`; the verdict field is only the short badge code.

## Review semantic Clusters

Raw NMF routes are numerical contribution patterns. The experiment handoff separately stores cluster_definitions: semantic cluster names, stories, graph_ids and example_graph_ids. Read scripts/read_evidence.py --section routes for the complete membership index and submitted definitions; use --ids GRAPH_ID ... for full member contexts and attribution vectors. Read the members supporting and challenging each story, including weak or mixed cases. Do not treat a route ID or its name as a semantic verdict.

A semantic cluster can combine members of several routes, and a raw route can contribute to several semantic clusters. Keep every measured member represented, retain counterexamples and uncertainty, and explain any semantic split within a raw route. Do not remove inconvenient members or narrow the displayed examples to conceal a failed generalization. Prefer a typical example plus any informative boundary or contrary case within the existing three-example display.

Keep the grouping compact: roughly ten to fourteen fine semantic groups for the whole neuron and six to eight reader-facing summary clusters are useful granularity targets, not hard limits. Do not promote incidental document topics, individual entities or single anomalous samples into independent neuron meanings. A separate meaning needs recurring evidence of a distinct response pattern. Preserve genuinely different patterns and every counterexample; use broad background or unresolved descriptions where evidence is weak.

For Inside the neuron, coordinates are measured raw gate and up; point colours show independent predictions from the frozen explanation. Read scripts/read_evidence.py --section response_predictions to inspect coverage, prediction-versus-measurement counts and full-prefix mistakes. Positive and negative truth are determined by measured product at the anchor; the predictor sees only the fixed explanation, its response_rules, text and anchor position. Distinguish feedback samples, already-seen evidence and experiments. Examine recurring strong mistakes and uncertain predictions before revising the claim; near-zero sign disagreements are weak evidence. Preserve counterexamples. Explain consequential mismatches and any resulting qualification in Criticism, using the actual feedback records.

Submit response_rules alongside the revised claim, retaining or revising the initial rules as evidence requires. Each has id, name, description and predicted_pole (positive, negative or uncertain); define textual conditions and anchor locations, not a measured-sign filter. The host freezes this submission, obtains blind predictions for it, and only then reveals a document-disjoint final holdout. Feedback supports revision; the final holdout evaluates the submitted explanation. Do not claim a final-holdout result before submission.

If the definitions remain supported, omit annotations.clusters: the existing memberships and examples are preserved even when routes or unit labels are edited. To revise semantic groups or their prose, submit the complete clusters array with id, name, story, graph_ids and example_graph_ids. The host recomputes numerical summaries from measured members. Raw route membership never changes. This review uses saved measurements only.

## Writing

Write a short title in the form “[concept] neuron”, with an optional phrase describing its response. Begin the explanation directly with what this neuron responds to or changes. Refer to the measured unit as “this neuron”; keep its layer and index in the identification fields.

Use ordinary descriptions of the positive and negative responses. Describe sparsity in the activation-distribution discussion, rather than calling the neuron a “sparse feature”. Keep qualifications in sentences instead of stacking them in a long title.

Describe the observations and conclusions directly for the reader.

Use approximate English word targets: lede 60–85; one_paragraph 150–180; negative_pole 80–120; what_would_change_my_mind 40–60. The latter three fields form The claim in detail. Activation spectrum summary is 35–55 words; Activation search summary is 45–70 words. Circuit introduction is approximately 30 words. Other section introductions are 25–50 words; cluster stories and figure captions are 35–65 words. Give the interpretation and decisive evidence rather than narrating experiment rounds or enumerating every result. Use short noun phrases for unit and group labels. Preserve contrary or unresolved cases in evidence, captions and Criticism results. These are writing targets, not truncation or acceptance rules.

Place direct output weights (Promotes/Suppresses) and neuron-ablation findings in annotations.sections.ablation (What it does). Use annotations.sections.circuit for upstream writers and downstream readers. The renderer places the numerical tables in those same sections.

## Measured quantities

Circuit tables store signed local RelP contributions: source activation times the modified derivative of the reader activation, with intervening MLP outputs detached. Upstream contributions are pooled over source positions; downstream measurements cover the nominated readers at the anchor position. The illustrated multi-hop graph additionally divides each local contribution by the receiver activation and multiplies by that receiver's influence on the graph root. These two displayed weight quantities are distinct. Route factorization uses sign-split, L1-normalized local contribution vectors.

skill_files.text:
# Report API

```bash
python scripts/write_report.py <<'JSON'
{"claim":{},"response_rules":[{"id":"rule_1","name":"Contextual condition","description":"Textual condition and anchor position predicting the response.","predicted_pole":"positive"}],"criticism":[],"annotations":{"figures":{},"graphs":{},"routes":{},"units":{},"sections":{}}}
JSON
```

Claim fields: title, lede, one_paragraph, negative_pole, what_would_change_my_mind, confidence.

Approximate English word targets: lede 60–85; one_paragraph 150–180; negative_pole 80–120; what_would_change_my_mind 40–60. The last three prose fields are the three paragraphs of The claim in detail. Do not pad a field to reach a target.

Each Criticism entry has round, attack, prediction, result, verdict, evidence. Put aggregates in result. Each evidence entry pairs text with an individual measured activation.

`verdict` is exactly one of `survived`, `narrowed`, or `rejected`, matching the three report badges. `survived` means the tested claim survived as written; `narrowed` means the finding requires a qualification or revision; `rejected` means the tested claim failed. Put the explanation of that decision in `result`, never in `verdict`. `attack` is the critic's challenge shown beside the badge; `prediction`, `result`, and individual evidence appear when the row is opened.

```json
{
  "criticism": [
    {
      "round": 1,
      "attack": "State the alternative explanation being tested.",
      "prediction": "State the contrasting predictions before reporting the measurements.",
      "result": "Explain the measured outcome and why it narrows the claim.",
      "verdict": "narrowed",
      "evidence": [{"text": "An actual measured example", "activation": 1.0}]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example is structural; use this run's actual text and measurements.

Annotations:

- headline_figure_id: the measured ten-condition common-frame sweep selected for the headline. Omit to preserve the experiment stage's choice.
- graph_ids: exactly three measured display-graph IDs in publication order. These come from multi-hop graphs, independently of the route-atlas IDs used in clusters.
- figures, keyed by experiment ID: title, rationale, caption.
- graphs, keyed by experiment ID: title, why, look_at (list).
- routes, keyed by measured route ID: name, description. These name the raw numerical patterns; they do not define semantic membership.
- clusters (optional): the complete array shown below. Omit to preserve the existing semantic groups and representative examples. Editing routes alone never replaces clusters.
- units, keyed by Lx_Ny: label string.
- sections, keyed by spectrum/search/clusters/anatomy/ablation/family/circuit/tests: summary. Spectrum is approximately 35–55 English words; search 45–70; Circuit approximately 30 words; other introductions 25–50. Anatomy may also include strip_caption. Captions and cluster stories are approximately 35–65 words. These are prose guidelines, not schema size limits.
- anatomy (optional): sentence, pairs and groups using the same saved-case selectors as the experiment skill. This changes the selected existing traces without a model call.

The renderer takes numerical values from saved measurements. Your annotations supply the interpretation. Blind maximum/minimum tests measure the incoming initial explanation. Inside the neuron uses a separate blind response prediction: its feedback is available for revision, while a final held-out set is revealed only after the revised claim and response_rules have been submitted. Submission runs an independent review and returns the rendered report path.

## Read evidence

```bash
python scripts/read_evidence.py --section index
python scripts/read_evidence.py --section response_predictions --limit 4
python scripts/read_evidence.py --section contexts --group bottom_tokens --limit 4
python scripts/read_evidence.py --section measurements
python scripts/read_evidence.py --section measurements --ids EXPERIMENT_ID
```

Replace EXPERIMENT_ID with an ID from the experiment list. Each experiment overview includes its recorded values, statistics, directory path and available JSON files. Complete measurements are in those files; load the relevant file and select the fields required for the analysis. The report HTML is generated by the host.


## Semantic cluster annotation

Read the incoming definitions with --section routes. Use --section routes --ids GRAPH_ID to read a complete measured member. The index includes all natural training route members, including low activations; its context_preview is only for navigation. graph_ids are measured graph identifiers, not case IDs. Counts, shares, member_routes, key units and example values are host-derived.

```json
{
  "annotations": {
    "clusters": [
      {
        "id": "c1",
        "name": "Supported semantic group",
        "story": "What the actual members share, which contribution patterns recur, and what remains contrary or unresolved.",
        "graph_ids": ["MEASURED_GRAPH_ID_A", "MEASURED_GRAPH_ID_B"],
        "example_graph_ids": ["MEASURED_GRAPH_ID_A", "MEASURED_GRAPH_ID_B"]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Replace all placeholders with measured IDs and evidence-supported prose. Include the other clusters as well when replacing the array. Keep every member represented; mixed or unresolved groups are permitted. Choose at most three examples per group, retaining informative exceptions. Do not add numeric values.

The response_predictions section returns the frozen explanation version, response_rules, separate feedback/seen/experiment summaries and paginated predictions joined to measured signs and activations. Cases are ordered with strong directional errors first. Use --ids, --group, --offset and --limit as needed. Revise response_rules together with the claim, even when retaining the same rule IDs.

# Report workflow

Read the previous stage at `/inputs/handoff/handoff.json` and `report/index.html`, then from this skill directory:

```bash
python scripts/write_report.py <<'JSON'
{"claim":{},"criticism":[],"annotations":{"figures":{},"graphs":{}}}
JSON
```

Fill the fields described in the API reference. Submission runs an independent review of the report, saves your interpretation and annotations, and renders the measured figures and graphs. Wait for the tool to return its report path.

## Long tools

Tool scripts wait for the operation to finish, then return its saved result. Continue only after that response.
